# Story 01 — Enhance Button component and action hierarchy patterns (Story: 11)

## Prerequisites

- Frontend workspace at `frontend/` builds and tests pass on `main` (last known-good after Story 8 completed the identity screens and Story 10 introduced the tokens/theme foundation used here). No other plans in `.squad/plans/` exist yet — this is the first planned story under the `some-enhancment` feature.
- Coordinate with owners of `frontend/src/features/identity/**` before changing the detail-page headers: those files were last touched by the identity-access FE story (see `.squad/stories/implement-identity-access-fe/5/intake.md`).
- Backend is out of scope; do not touch anything under `backend/`.

---

## Story Goal

Consolidate the button visual system and the action hierarchy across the product so that (1) every screen shows at most one primary action, (2) peer actions in the same context share one variant and size, (3) destructive actions are never the most prominent element in a list row, and (4) the solid `danger` variant appears only inside a confirmation dialog. The `Button` component itself and the list-page row hierarchy were already brought in line by earlier stories; the remaining work is to **close the gaps in the detail-page hierarchy, add the missing guardrail/regression tests for AC2/AC6/AC8/AC10/AC12, and finish the living-doc coverage on `TokensPage`**.

Explicitly **not in scope**: split buttons, segmented controls (the language switcher lives in DS-5), floating action buttons, and any changes to the visual tokens (owned by Story 10).

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour that must be preserved:** row actions use `tertiary` sm for View/Edit and `danger-subtle` sm for Delete; the create button in each list page header is the sole `primary` action for that view; `ConfirmDialog` renders `[Cancel][Confirm]` in DOM order and flips visually under RTL via CSS.
- **New behaviour introduced by this story:** detail pages must expose a proper page header with a single `primary` action (Edit) and a visually separated destructive action (`danger-subtle`), matching the intake's "Detail page header" row; add guardrail tests for AC2/AC6/AC8/AC10/AC12; extend TokensPage docs with a rendered example of the loading-width-preservation and the icon-only hit-target size.

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Detail page headers: enforce one primary + ghost group + separated danger-subtle

**File: `frontend/src/features/identity/users/UserDetailsPage.tsx`**

Restructure the render output so the first block is a page header with:

- an `<h1>` on the reading-start side,
- a `Button variant="primary"` "Edit" action gated by `PermissionGate permission="User.Update"`, end-aligned,
- a **visually separated** `Button variant="danger-subtle"` "Delete" action to the reading-end of the primary, only inside `PermissionGate permission="User.Delete"`, keeping the existing `disabled={isSelf}` + `disabledReason={isSelf ? t('admin.common.actions.reason.cannotDeleteSelf') : undefined}` (see current lines 71–79).

Move the existing `<UserRoleAssignModal>` and `<ConfirmDialog>` unchanged. The `Button variant="secondary"` "Manage roles" action inside the roles section (current lines 65–67) stays as-is: it is a secondary action inside a card, not a peer of the header primary.

Add a new **`UserDetailsPage.module.css`** with a `.pageHeader` grid that mirrors `UserListPage.module.css`'s `.pageHeader` (start/end flex row with `gap: var(--space-3)`, `flex-wrap: wrap`) and a `.headerActions` cluster with `gap: var(--space-2)`; add a divider (`border-inline-start: 1px solid var(--color-border-subtle); padding-inline-start: var(--space-3)`) on the destructive-action wrapper for the "visually separated" requirement. **All values from tokens** — no raw px/hex, so `layer.test.ts` continues to pass.

Do **not** introduce a solid `variant="danger"` button here — only `ConfirmDialog` may carry it. The existing `<ConfirmDialog … variant="danger">` at lines 88–96 remains the sole destructive-confirm surface.

**File: `frontend/src/features/identity/roles/RoleDetailsPage.tsx`**

Reuse the existing role delete confirmation dialog (or add one modelled on `RoleListPage.tsx` lines 111–119 if none exists). No `disabledReason` for roles unless the role is a system role — leave as `undefined` if there is no existing self-referential guard.

### 3 — Guardrail tests

**File: `frontend/src/features/identity/__tests__/dangerVariantHierarchy.test.ts`**

Extend this existing file (do not rename it) with two additional guardrail tests inside the same `describe`, following the same `collectTsxFiles(FEATURES_ROOT)` + regex-source scan style used at ~lines 9–24.

1. **`it('AC2 — at most one <Button variant="primary"> per top-level *Page.tsx file')`.** For each `*Page.tsx` under `src/features/**` (excluding `design-system` and `__tests__`), count matches of `variant="primary"` on `<Button` opening tags (reuse `OPENING_TAG_PATTERN`). Assert the count is ≤ 1 per file. Record any file with > 1 in a `violations` array and assert `expect(violations).toEqual([])`. Note in a comment that this test is a static approximation — a page that renders two variants of the same button under mutually exclusive conditions is a false positive and must be exempted by name in an `EXEMPTIONS` set at the top; keep the set empty for now.
2. **`it('AC4 — row action columns never render <Button variant="primary"> or <Button variant="danger">')`.** For each file matching `**/features/**/*ListPage.tsx`, extract the source of any object literal whose `key` is `'actions'` (or a `render:` function that returns View/Edit/Delete) and assert neither `variant="primary"` nor `variant="danger"` appears inside that block. A pragmatic implementation is to slice from the string `key: 'actions'` up to the matching `},` — accept that this is fragile and document the assumption in a comment.

**File: `frontend/src/shared/components/button/Button.test.tsx`**

Add three tests inside the existing `describe('Button', …)`:

1. **AC6 — loading preserves width.** Render `<Button loading>Save changes</Button>` and `<Button>Save changes</Button>` back-to-back in the same container; assert both buttons have the same `offsetWidth` (fall back to comparing `getBoundingClientRect().width` under jsdom). 2. **AC8 — icon-only min hit target is at least 32×32.** Assert the raw CSS source (`buttonCss` at the top of the file) contains `min-inline-size: var(--space-7)` and `min-block-size: var(--space-7)` inside the `[data-icon-only='true']` block. `--space-7` resolves to `32px` per `frontend/src/shared/theme/tokens.ts`; add a matching cross-check assertion that resolves `--space-7` from `lightTheme` to `32px`.
3. **AC9 — focus-visible uses the focus token on every variant.** Assert `buttonCss` contains `outline: var(--focus-ring)` inside a `:focus-visible` rule and does not contain any `data-variant='…' … outline:` override.

**File: `frontend/src/shared/components/overlay/ConfirmDialog.test.tsx`**

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **A page renders a primary button conditionally in two branches.** The AC2 static guardrail (Task 3) will fire a false positive. Mitigation: the `EXEMPTIONS` set at the top of `dangerVariantHierarchy.test.ts`; empty for now, document the escape hatch in a comment above it. Enforcement point: the guardrail test itself.
- **A future page adds a solid `danger` button outside a `ConfirmDialog`.** Caught by the existing AC5 test at `frontend/src/features/identity/__tests__/dangerVariantHierarchy.test.ts:32-49`.
- **Icon-only button without `aria-label` in production.** The `import.meta.env.DEV` warn at `Button.tsx:49-51` catches this in dev; the icon-only usage in `TokensPage.tsx:145-147` already supplies `aria-label={t('common.moreActions')}`. Reviewer must verify any new icon-only usage in Task 1.
- **Delete-self on the detail page.** `UserDetailsPage.tsx` already gates the delete button with `disabled={isSelf}` and `disabledReason={t('admin.common.actions.reason.cannotDeleteSelf')}` at lines 74–76; retain this exact wiring when moving the button into the new header.
- **RTL browser without `:dir()` support.** The fallback `[dir='rtl'] .actions` rule in `ConfirmDialog.module.css:15-17` covers this; the AC10 CSS-source test at `ConfirmDialog.test.tsx:67-69` locks it.
- **Arabic label wider than the button under an `sm` size in a table row.** Buttons are content-sized (no fixed width; see `.button` in `Button.module.css:1-20`) and the row layout uses `<Table>` cells that grow to content. If a future column ever caps widths, Task 4's render test won't catch a table-level truncation — document as a known gap in the test file's top comment.
- **Reduced-motion users.** `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` at `Button.module.css:162-168` shortens transitions and spins; the existing test at `Button.test.tsx:110-112` locks the block's presence. Do not remove.
- **Consumer sets `disabled` but forgets `disabledReason`.** `hasReason` becomes `false`; no `aria-describedby` or `title` is emitted (see `Button.tsx:47`, `Button.test.tsx:80-85`). This is intentional: the reason is optional, but permission-gated actions on the identity pages already pass it.

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend runs:** from `frontend/`, `pnpm install` (only if lockfile changed), then `pnpm vitest run` — all suites green.
2. **Frontend typecheck:** from `frontend/`, `pnpm tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`.
3. **Frontend lint:** from `frontend/`, `pnpm eslint . --max-warnings 0`.
4. **Frontend build:** from `frontend/`, `pnpm build`.
5. **Manual — LTR:** `pnpm dev`, sign in, navigate to `/admin/users`, confirm row actions are `[View] [Edit] [Delete-outlined-red]` all at the same visual weight (`sm`), and that only the header "Create user" is solid. Open a user's detail page, confirm the new header has `[H1 title] … [Edit primary] │ [Delete danger-subtle]` with a divider between the ghost group and the destructive action. Click Delete → confirmation dialog shows `[Cancel] [Confirm-solid-red]` on the right.
6. **Manual — RTL:** switch the app language to Arabic (existing switcher in the header), repeat step 5. The header primary sits on the reading-end (left in RTL), the confirmation dialog's Confirm button appears on the reading-end (left) with DOM order unchanged.
7. **Manual — reduced motion:** OS-level enable "reduce motion", hover a primary button — transition duration collapses to ~0ms, the loading spinner still visibly rotates but at the reduced duration.
8. **Regression:** run the identity module tests explicitly: `pnpm vitest run src/features/identity src/shared/components/button src/shared/components/overlay src/features/design-system`.
